page: Microsoft Azure E96ias_v4 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for enterprise workloads requiring substantial memory footprints and high parallel processing capability. Powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7452 processor operating at up to 3.35 GHz, the instance delivers 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled on the x86_64 architecture. The platform includes 672 GB of system memory, providing 7 GB of RAM per vCPU, along with 1,443 GB of local SSD temporary storage. It operates without dedicated GPU hardware accelerators and is managed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results demonstrate strengths in multi-threaded execution and cryptographic processing. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top-tier results in PassMark CPU encryption tests with hardware AES and SHA support, alongside strong results in PassMark CPU overall scoring, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Clang compilation tasks. Cached memory bandwidth reaches 3,921.34 GB/s for small blocks, complementing an in-memory Redis SET benchmark exceeding 72.45 million operations per second. However, single-core CPU throughput is constrained, as shown by lower-tier rankings in single-core stress-ng tests, indicating that tasks dependent on aggressive per-thread clock speeds face performance ceilings.

The hardware configuration provides high resource density for organizations running heavy in-memory data structures, large database engines, and intensive batch processing. The inclusion of 1,443 GB of local solid-state storage supports high-speed caching and intermediate data stages. While unsuitable for single-threaded processing or large-scale AI generation tasks—where 70B parameter LLM inference achieves only 4.45 prompt tokens per second—the E96ias_v4 offers an efficient allocation of compute and memory capacity for large-scale enterprise databases, distributed caching, and parallel build pipelines.

Built on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it couples 672 GB of RAM (7 GB per vCPU) with 1,443 GB of local SSD storage and zero discrete GPUs. Benchmark data highlights top-tier cryptographic acceleration, strong multi-core decompression throughput, and high-velocity in-memory Redis operations exceeding 72 million operations per second. The substantial memory footprint and high parallel core count make the E96ias_v4 well structured for memory-intensive enterprise databases, distributed caching layers, and high-throughput compilation or batch-processing pipelines.
